title: Make the steward an agent that reads Athena broadly and queues work
summary: Replace the steward's built-in failure counting with a model-backed agent run: the stored short, stable prompt becomes the system prompt, and the agent gets read-only access to code, prompts, briefs, records, git history and GitHub CI/PRs/deploys (via gh), then returns work items and ladder-gated changes that Athena queues. The audience is the Athena owner, who judges whether the steward now reasons over Athena and steers it as the 2026-10-14 BRIEF addendum describes.

defaults_applied.how: Fake-driver tests for the steward run and policy tests; cargo test and clippy must pass.
Read-only access is enforced by the tool policy hook, and the ladder limit by decide(), not by prompt text.
The steward's prompt reaching nothing is fixed by wiring a model call, not by editing the prompt text.
Docs and changelog explain the steward for an outside reader.
Reuse the existing AgentDriver, policy and gh CLI rather than a GitHub client crate.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The agent runs through the existing AgentDriver and Claude Code headless path, so it is budgeted, hermetic and recorded; the driver must be made available to the background thread (e.g. shared via Arc or a fresh driver built from wiring).
A new Role variant (steward) or reuse of an existing one is chosen by the producer; adding a variant requires updating exhaustive matches, scoring and invariants that treat reader specially.
GitHub data is fetched where it lives by read-only gh commands inside the agent's policy, not stored in Athena; a missing gh or network is a blind spot, not an error.
The stored prompt stays short and stable; if its text changes it is a new role version (steward-2) per roles.rs convention.
Cadence (every five finished tasks) and the ladder limit (defaults-conventions) are kept unchanged; BRIEF says no triggers beyond the parallel loop.
records/ is not edited directly by the producer; steward output lands through the existing committer.

acceptance_criteria.text: steward::run invokes an AgentDriver with the stored STEWARD_PROMPT as the system prompt (via the role definition, unchanged in meaning) and records that invocation (role, usage, cost) like other roles' invocations; the call site in note_finished still runs in the background and never blocks the main flow.

The steward's invocation is read-only: its tool policy allows reading the repository snapshot, records, prompts, briefs and git history (git log/show/diff) plus read-only GitHub queries (gh run/pr/api GET for CI, PRs, deploys), and denies writes, pushes, and mutating gh/git commands; policy tests cover both allowed and denied cases.

The agent returns structured output (work items with kind, key, title, rung, source and evidence references, and a request text); Athena validates it, then still routes every item through decide(): rungs at or below the role's limit queue a request via RequestQueue, higher rungs (owner goals, brief requirements, design decisions) queue only a proposal with evidence.

Each source the agent reports it could not read (including GitHub when gh or network is unavailable) becomes a blind-spot work item naming that source; items whose key already exists in records are not queued twice.

The old repeated_failures counting is no longer the steward's only reasoning: it is either removed or provided to the agent as input, and docs/design/roles-and-ladder.md and CHANGELOG.md say the steward now calls a model.

Run `cargo test` (including crates/athena-cli/tests/steward.rs using the fake driver): a steward run with a scripted fake agent output commits the expected work items and queued request, makes no commit when the output is empty, and a nested run makes no real model call.
Run `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`: both are clean.

out_of_scope: Changing BRIEF.md, athena.toml, defaults.toml or CI workflows
Adding new steward cadence triggers or a second role
Storing GitHub data in Athena's records (it is pulled as needed)
Letting the steward edit files directly instead of queueing requests
Changing the ladder's rungs or the may_change rule
departures: Larger than typical jobs: new model-backed role touching agent driver, tool policy, records, scoring and background threading, so cost, time and failure risk are above the reference.
